prompt:
Replace the single standing pose in image 1 with an eight frame WALK CYCLE.
Use image 1 only as the character identity reference.
Do not repeat the reference standing pose. Preserve this exact male technician identity,
pixel art style, blue hard hat, ear defenders, lime vest, orange trim, silver
bands, long slate sleeves, blue jeans, brown boots, and right hip tool pouch.
Do not introduce a different character or a different illustration style.

Draw the leg and arm sequence as eight distinct phases of a complete
RIGHT FACING PROFILE walk cycle. The near leg must actually move from front
to back in the first half and from back to front in the second half.
Keep the far leg visibly behind it at overlaps. Preserve the outfit on each
side rather than mirroring the whole character.

Use an exact 4 column by 2 row grid on a 2048 by 1024 transparent canvas.
Each 512 by 512 cell contains one complete figure. Read left to right, top
row first. In every cell keep the pelvis centered at x=256, the grounded boot
sole at y=480, and the standing height at 420 pixels. Use one shared scale.
Keep all pixels within the cell. Keep the head and torso registered between
cells; only a small vertical weight shift is allowed, not horizontal drift.

Frame 1: near leg forward heel contact, far leg extended behind on its toe.
Frame 2: weight settles onto the near foot, near knee bends slightly; the far
foot lifts behind and begins swinging forward.
Frame 3: PASSING. The near leg supports directly beneath the hip. The far knee
passes the near knee, and its foot is lifted from the floor. This is NOT a
wide stride or a second contact pose.
Frame 4: near foot rolls onto the toe behind the hip, far knee and lower leg
reach forward but the far heel is still just above the floor.
Frame 5: far leg forward heel contact, near leg extended behind on its toe.
This reverses which anatomical leg leads compared with frame 1.
Frame 6: weight settles onto the far foot, far knee bends slightly; the near
foot lifts behind and begins swinging forward.
Frame 7: PASSING. The far leg supports directly beneath the hip. The near knee
passes the far knee with the near foot lifted, not extended to the front.
Frame 8: far foot rolls onto its toe behind the hip; near lower leg reaches
forward, near heel almost touching, ready to continue directly into frame 1.

Swing the arms opposite their legs. Hands are empty; tools remain on the belt.
Preserve adult proportions, head size, body volume, square pixel clusters,
stepped outlines, and the existing material palette. Never resize each pose.
No blurry outlines, antialiasing, motion trails, added scenery, ground shadows,
checkerboards, text, numbered cells, borders, or painted backgrounds.
Output real transparent RGBA. Image 2 is the authoritative pose guide. Match each of its eight separate limb poses in the corresponding cell. Cyan marks the near arm and leg. Purple marks the far arm and leg. These guide colors identify limbs only; render all clothing in the normal outfit colors from image 1, not cyan or purple. Image 1 supplies identity and pixel style only. Image 2 supplies the exact movement, opposite arm swing, bent knee passing poses, and front-to-back leg alternation. Replace the colored stick figures with the technician, not copies of the first pose.
purpose: Eight frame right facing walk with alternating near and far legs.
phases: Near heel contacts; far foot pushes off behind.
Near leg supports; far foot lifts behind.
Near leg supports below the hip; far knee passes forward.
Near toe pushes off; far foot reaches forward.
Far heel contacts; near foot pushes off behind.
Far leg supports; near foot lifts behind.
Far leg supports below the hip; near knee passes forward.
Far toe pushes off; near foot reaches forward.
postprocessing: Whole sheet candidates repeated the same anatomical leg and were rejected.
Masked edits corrected individual poses 4 through 8 using the colored limb guide.
The final source keeps unmasked pixels from the selected whole sheet candidate.
Generated edits shortened supporting legs. The source edit restores lower body extent from the pelvis to one shared source floor baseline without moving the torso.
Canonical source cells remain 512x512. Runtime normalization uses one fixed 512-to-171 scale and the published animation palette.
Map canonical source pixels to this hero's walking color ramps from commit 15a3bf1 before runtime normalization.
Generator records below describe the base image and masked edits, not a single generation of the final composite.
Intermediate crop and mask paths are logical provenance names; their original input hashes are retained.
